question: In which year was the Competition Act passed by the Parliament in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2002**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Competition Act** was passed by the **Parliament of India in 2002** and came into effect on **13 January 2003**.
 
• This act was enacted to replace the **Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act, 1969 (MRTP Act)**, which had become outdated in addressing the modern economic framework and competition issues.
 
• The **Competition Commission of India (CCI)** was established under this act to promote competition, prevent practices that have an adverse effect on competition, and protect the interests of consumers.
 
• The act focuses on **prohibition of anti-competitive agreements, abuse of dominant position, and regulation of combinations (mergers and acquisitions)** that may harm competition.
 
• The **Competition Act, 2002**, aligns India’s economic regulations with the liberalized and globalized economic environment of the 21st century, promoting fair competition in the market.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Objectives of the Competition Act, 2002:**

 
 
• To prevent practices that have an **adverse effect on competition**.
 
• To promote and sustain **competition in markets**.
 
• To protect the **interests of consumers**.
 
• To ensure **freedom of trade** carried on by participants in markets in India.
 
 
 
• **Competition Commission of India (CCI):**
 
 
• The CCI is a **statutory body** established under the Competition Act, 2002.
 
• It is tasked with eliminating practices that affect competition and regulating mergers or acquisitions to ensure they do not harm market competition.
 
• The CCI comprises a **Chairperson and 6 members**, appointed by the Central Government.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the Competition Act:**
 
 
• It **prohibits anti-competitive agreements**, such as cartels, that can harm competition.
 
• It addresses the **abuse of dominant position** by enterprises, ensuring that no entity exploits its market power unfairly.
 
• It regulates **mergers, acquisitions, and combinations** to prevent concentration of market power.
 
 
 
• **Replacement of MRTP Act:**
 
 
• The **Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices (MRTP) Act** of 1969 aimed to curb monopolistic practices but was deemed inadequate for a liberalized economic environment.
 
• The Competition Act, 2002, was introduced to address modern economic challenges like globalization and ensure fair competition.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• The act fosters a **healthy competitive environment**, ensuring efficiency and innovation in the market.
 
• It enhances **consumer welfare** by ensuring fair pricing and quality products.
 
• The act plays a pivotal role in preventing exploitation by monopolies or cartels.
